title: 🔐 "App Lock" returns to Pixel phones — lock any app with your fingerprint or PIN!
body: 🔐 "App Lock" returns to Pixel phones — lock any app with your fingerprint or PIN!
The "App Lock" feature returned to Google's Pixel phones, after a long absence, in the new beta version "Android 17 QPR3".
The feature lets you lock any app with a PIN or your fingerprint, so only you can open it, even if your phone is unlocked in someone else's hand.
The wide, stable release of the feature is expected in the first quarter of 2027 — within the first months of next year.
The idea is simple but important: your photos, messages and banking apps deserve an extra lock, even if your phone itself is locked with a code.
Many of us lend our phone to a friend to view a photo or make a call, without wanting them to wander through the rest of our apps.
Simply put: imagine every room in your house having its own lock, not just the front door. That is what "App Lock" does to your phone.
Do you prefer an extra lock on your sensitive apps, or is locking the phone itself enough for you?
